title: Crestline Trip Credit in Place of a Cash Refund — Basis Questions
content:
This page covers the choice a customer of Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers may make to take a Crestline Trip Credit in place of a cash refund of a ticket.

**The rule.** A customer who is entitled to a cash refund of a ticket may choose a Crestline Trip Credit instead, issued on the ground of refund alternative. A customer is entitled where a refundable fare brand was cancelled voluntarily, or where an involuntary refund is due under the ticket rules of Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand. The Trip Credit's face value is the refundable amount plus a bonus of 10 percent of that amount, and the bonus is capped at 100 US dollars. The choice is the customer's alone and is made before the refund is paid. Once a refund payout exists for the ticket, the Trip Credit is no longer available. A customer who is not entitled to a refund receives a Crestline Flight Credit under the cancellation rule and never a bonus.

## Basis questions

**Whose decision is it?**
The customer's alone. The customer's own statement of the choice, for the ticket concerned, is what counts.

**When must the choice be made?**
Before the refund is paid. What decides this is whether the ticket's transaction record already shows a refund payout. Once a refund payout exists for that ticket, the Trip Credit is no longer available.

**How is the face value made up?**
The face value is the refundable amount, plus 10 percent of that amount as a bonus, with the bonus never more than 100 US dollars.

**What does a customer who is not entitled to a refund receive?**
A Crestline Flight Credit under the cancellation rule, without any bonus.

## Worked values (hypothetical refundable amounts)

| Refundable amount (USD) | 10 percent of the amount | Bonus after the cap of 100 | Trip Credit face value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 420.00 | 42.00 | 42.00 | 462.00 |
| 1,000.00 | 100.00 | 100.00 | 1,100.00 |
| 1,200.00 | 120.00 | 100.00 | 1,300.00 |
